title: Troubleshooting
text: Start with juphyter doctor. It names the failing part, and for a Python on the wrong PATH it prints the export line that fixes it.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
A kernel stopped working
The kernel records absolute paths to a PHP binary, a Python interpreter, and juphyter itself. Upgrading or removing any of them breaks the kernel, and juphyter doctor marks it fail.

Run juphyter install again with the same --name to record the current paths.
A kernel installed into a project breaks when the project’s vendor directory is deleted. Run composer install in the project, or uninstall the kernel.

title: Troubleshooting
section: No Python can host the kernel
text:
No Python can host the kernel
juphyter install looks for an interpreter in this order: the one named by --python, then the one that owns the jupyter command on PATH. When that interpreter has no ipykernel 7, it builds a virtual environment with JupyterLab instead of installing into it.

System and Homebrew Python builds are externally managed, and pip install into them refuses. The virtual environment avoids that.
An environment that already exists at the --create-venv path is reused, and its packages are installed again, so a second run finishes an interrupted one.
A directory at that path that holds something other than an environment is refused.
With --python, the command builds nothing. When the named interpreter has no ipykernel, it prints the pip install command for that interpreter and writes no kernel.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
The stop button does nothing
The PHP binary that runs the cells lacks pcntl, or lists its functions in disable_functions. juphyter doctor reports it as a warning. Enable pcntl for that binary, or run juphyter install --php with a binary that has it. Limitations covers what an interrupt can and cannot stop.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Quarto

Quarto cannot find the kernel
ERROR: Jupyter kernel 'php' not found. Known kernels: python3
Quarto’s interpreter has no Jupyter in it, so it can list no kernels. juphyter doctor reports this as Quarto: not ready. and prints the fix. Python interpreters and editors covers how to point Quarto at an interpreter that has Jupyter.


KeyError: 'path' with a kernelspec block
Quarto accepts the fuller front matter that Jupyter writes into a notebook, but for juphyter it also needs path, the directory that holds kernel.json:
---
jupyter:
  kernelspec:
    name: php85
    language: php
    display_name: "PHP 8.5"
    path: /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels/php85
---
Quarto reads path to look for a setup cell beside the kernelspec, which it does for any language it has no built-in support for. jupyter: php85 fills it in, so name the kernel instead of describing it.


Unknown message type: 'comm_open'
Every render prints this once. It comes from ipykernel, because the kernel installs no comm manager, and it has no effect on the rendered document. The same absence is why ipywidgets are unsupported.


A new PHP session on every render
Quarto keeps a kernel alive between renders only for languages it can write a setup or cleanup cell for. It has none for PHP, and juphyter install writes none, so each render starts a new PHP session, including with --execute-daemon.


Rendering frozen documents
Quarto looks up a document’s kernel by name before it reads frozen output, so a kernel with that name has to be registered on the rendering machine even when no cell runs. Contributing shows how this repository renders its own site that way.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
Two Python interpreters take part in running a PHP document:
The environment that juphyter install --create-venv builds has all of these, because it holds JupyterLab. JupyterLab starts each kernel with the interpreter its kernelspec names, so it needs no further setup.
When Quarto’s interpreter has no Jupyter, a render stops with Jupyter kernel 'php' not found. Point Quarto at the environment with one of the fixes below.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
How Quarto chooses an interpreter
In Quarto 1.10.18, the version CI tests, the first match wins:







Order
Source




1
QUARTO_PYTHON in the environment


2
QUARTO_PYTHON in a project _environment file beside _quarto.yml


3
The first python3 on PATH



Quarto does not read VIRTUAL_ENV, does not fall back to python, and ignores RETICULATE_PYTHON.
juphyter doctor prints the interpreter Quarto will use in its Quarto section. quarto check jupyter 2>&1 reports it from Quarto’s side, and a Jupyter: (None) line means that interpreter has no Jupyter.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
At a terminal
For the current shell, put the environment first on PATH with the export line that juphyter doctor prints, or activate it:
source ~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/activate
quarto render notebook.qmd
For one command:
QUARTO_PYTHON=~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python quarto render notebook.qmd
For every render in one Quarto project, put an _environment file beside _quarto.yml, with an absolute path:
QUARTO_PYTHON=/Users/you/.venvs/juphyter/bin/python
Setting QUARTO_PYTHON or the environment’s PATH entry in a shell startup file changes the interpreter for every Quarto project on the machine. juphyter writes neither to a startup file.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
VS Code and Cursor

Open the document’s folder as a workspace. A .qmd opened on its own has no workspace folder for the Quarto extension to ask about.
Run Python: Select Interpreter and choose an environment that has Jupyter, such as ~/.venvs/juphyter.

The Quarto extension passes that choice to Quarto as QUARTO_PYTHON on every render in the workspace, so a project _environment file cannot override it. Correct a wrong selection in the interpreter picker.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
Positron
The steps are the same as in VS Code: open the folder, then run Python: Select Interpreter.

A workspace that already has an interpreter stored keeps it. python.defaultInterpreterPath in .vscode/settings.json applies only when none has been selected.
A change to that setting takes effect after Developer: Reload Window.
Each render opens a new terminal, where echo "QUARTO_PYTHON=[$QUARTO_PYTHON]" shows the interpreter Positron passed. An empty value means none is selected.

title: Python interpreters and editors
text:
Other editors
An editor without Quarto integration, such as PhpStorm or RStudio, leaves the choice to PATH. Activate the environment before starting the editor, or set QUARTO_PYTHON in its terminal or run configuration. Quarto does not read the Python preference that RStudio stores.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Start JupyterLab from the Python environment that has it:
~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab
The launcher lists each kernel juphyter registered under its display name, such as “PHP 8.5” for the default php kernel and “PHP (phpstats)” for the kernel from Installation. A notebook that is already open changes kernel through Kernel > Change Kernel.
JupyterLab finds kernels in the per-user Jupyter data directory and in JUPYTER_DATA_DIR when it is set. jupyter kernelspec list shows the kernels a JupyterLab started from the same environment will find.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Start JupyterLab from the Python environment that has it:
~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab
The launcher lists each kernel juphyter registered under its display name, such as “PHP 8.5” for the default php kernel and “PHP (phpstats)” for the kernel from Installation. A notebook that is already open changes kernel through Kernel > Change Kernel.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Running cells
A cell’s result appears under it as Out[n]. State carries from one cell to the next. The stop button interrupts a running cell when PHP has the pcntl extension, and Kernel > Restart Kernel starts a new PHP session with nothing defined.
Tab completion covers three cases:

Variables in the session, after a $.
Declared functions and classes, for a bare prefix.
Public methods, properties, and constants, after -> or ::.

An unfinished block or string keeps the cell open for another line instead of running it.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Project classes
Jupyter starts the kernel in the notebook’s directory. The kernel looks upward from there for vendor/autoload.php, so a notebook saved inside a Composer project can use that project’s classes and packages.
A notebook kept outside the project it works on names the autoloader in a juphyter.json beside it:
{
  "autoload": "../app/vendor/autoload.php"
}
Which classes a notebook sees lists every way to set it.

title: JupyterLab
text:

A phiz plot appears as a chart. JupyterLab draws it from its Vega-Lite specification and needs no extension.

title: JupyterLab
text:
Converting a notebook
quarto convert turns a .ipynb into a .qmd and back, and jupyter nbconvert exports a notebook to HTML or PDF. Both work on a PHP notebook, because they read the notebook file format and not the language.

title: juphyter
text:
Run PHP in Jupyter notebooks and Quarto documents, with tables and charts displayed alongside code.
A notebook is a file of cells, each holding a few lines of code with its output beneath it. The program that runs the cells is a kernel. juphyter is a kernel for PHP, and it keeps one PHP session open, so a variable set in one cell is available in the next.

title: juphyter
text:
What a cell shows
The value of a cell’s last expression is its output. A phibble data frame appears as an HTML table with its dimensions and column types, and a phiz plot appears as a chart. Other values appear as a compact dump.
The examples below use phibble, phplyr, and phiz. In a Composer project, install them with the command below. The php kernel then loads the project’s vendor/autoload.php for any notebook or document inside the project. The phpstats packages covers using them outside a project.
composer require phpstats/phibble phpstats/phplyr phpstats/phiz
phplyr’s round() replaces PHP’s built-in round() in the cells after this import.

use function Phplyr\{phplyr, group_by, summarize, arrange, desc, n, mean, round};

title: juphyter
text:
What the kernel provides

State across cells, including use imports and declared functions and classes.
Tracebacks that name the cell and the line, instead of eval()'d code.
HTML tables for phibble data frames and charts for phiz plots, plus toHtml() and toMimeBundle() hooks for any other class.
Juphyter\display(), which shows a value part way through a cell.
Completion of variables, functions, classes, and members.
Interrupting a running cell with the stop button, when PHP has the pcntl extension.
Loading the nearest vendor/autoload.php above the notebook, so a notebook inside a Composer project can use that project’s classes and packages.

juphyter requires none of the phpstats packages. It runs plain PHP, and it formats a phibble data frame or a phiz plot when those packages are installed.

title: juphyter
text:
How it works
A Python program built on ipykernel handles the Jupyter protocol, and a PHP process runs the cells. They talk over a Unix socket. That is why an install needs Python as well as PHP, and why the kernel runs on macOS and Linux only.
Installation covers the requirements and the install commands, and Getting started walks through a first notebook.

title: Show a table and a chart in a notebook

title: Contributing
text:
git clone https://github.com/phpstats/juphyter
cd juphyter
composer install
bin/juphyter runs the checkout. bin/juphyter install --name juphyter-dev registers a kernel that runs it, without replacing the php kernel.

title: Contributing
text:
Tests
The PHP tests and the coding standard:
vendor/bin/pest
composer lint
A few tests send the engine an interrupt and are skipped when PHP lacks the pcntl or posix extension. CI runs the PHP tests on PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5, on Ubuntu and macOS.
The protocol tests start the kernel and drive it over the Jupyter protocol. They need a Python with Jupyter:
python -m pip install -r tests/Protocol/requirements.txt
python -m pytest tests/Protocol
The render tests run Quarto on the documents in tests/Quarto/fixture. They need Quarto, PHP 8.5, and a Python with the packages in tests/Quarto/requirements.txt, and they install phibble, phplyr, and phiz from tests/Quarto/fixture/composer.json into build/:
python -m pip install -r tests/Quarto/requirements.txt
python -m pytest tests/Quarto
.github/workflows/family.yml runs the display formatter tests with the current Packagist releases of phibble, phplyr, and phiz installed. None of the three is a dependency of juphyter.

title: Contributing
text:
Documentation
The documentation is a Quarto site in docs/, and most pages run their PHP cells through the kernel. phpstats.org imports the rendered HTML from this repository and does not run Quarto, so the rendered pages and the frozen output under docs/_freeze/ are committed with their sources.
scripts/render-docs
The script installs phibble, phplyr, and phiz into build/docs/sandbox from the render tests’ manifest, registers a php kernel in a private Jupyter data directory under build/docs, renders every page through it, and copies the result into docs/. It needs PHP 8.5, because the overview uses the pipe operator. --refresh reinstalls the sandbox and the kernel. scripts/render-docs --help lists the environment variables that choose the PHP and the Python.
An executing render changes the committed HTML and frozen output even when no source changed, because Quarto gives each executed cell a new random id.
scripts/render-docs --frozen
renders from the frozen output with no PHP. Quarto looks up each page’s kernel by name before it reads frozen output, so the script registers a php kernel whose command exits immediately, and a page that needs executing fails the render. CI uses this to check that the committed HTML matches the sources.
A page joins the site through the sidebar in docs/_quarto.yml. phpstats.org takes its navigation from that sidebar and fails to sync a page that is listed without rendered HTML. site/site.json holds the install commands, requirements, and summary that phpstats.org shows on the package’s overview.
Plans and design notes are kept in docs/work/, outside the site.

title: Contributing
text:
The PHAR
php scripts/build-phar.php
writes build/juphyter.phar from the files listed in phar.json. php juphyter.phar install registers a kernel whose engine is the PHAR, and copies the Python transport beside the kernelspec, because Python cannot import from inside a PHAR. No PHAR is published with a release.

title: Getting started
text:
This page assumes the php kernel is installed and juphyter doctor reports it as ready. Installation covers both. The examples were run in a Quarto document, and they behave the same way in a JupyterLab notebook.
To follow along in JupyterLab, run jupyter lab from an environment that has it, such as ~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab, and choose the PHP kernel in the launcher. To follow along in Quarto, create a file first.qmd:
Then run quarto render first.qmd, which writes first.html.

Imports
A use statement applies to its own cell and to every later cell. A notebook can put its imports in its first cell and use short names afterward. This example uses phibble, which the php kernel finds when the document sits inside a Composer project that requires it, or which the phpstats kernel from Installation provides.

    ['channel' => 'store', 'region' => 'north', 'total' => 80.00],

title: Getting started
text:
Errors
A cell that throws shows the exception, its message, and a traceback whose lines name the cell and the line number.

$mean = fn (array $values) => array_sum($values) / count($values);

$mean([]);

DivisionByZeroError: Division by zero
DivisionByZeroError: Division by zero
  in a closure
  at Cell 5, line 3


The session survives the exception. Variables defined before it keep their values.
Warnings, notices, and deprecations appear in the cell’s error output, and the cell keeps running.

$widths = ['narrow' => 4, 'wide' => 12];

$widths['narrow'] + $widths['medium'];

Warning: Undefined array key "medium" in Cell 6, line 3


4

title: Installation
text:
Install juphyter
Install juphyter for your user and put Composer’s bin directory on PATH:
composer global require phpstats/juphyter
export PATH="$(composer global config bin-dir --absolute):$PATH"

title: Installation
text:
Register the kernel
juphyter install --create-venv ~/.venvs/juphyter
export PATH="$HOME/.venvs/juphyter/bin:$PATH"

juphyter install registers a kernel named php for your user, so one install serves notebooks and documents in every directory.
It uses the Python environment that owns the jupyter command on PATH when that environment has ipykernel. Otherwise it builds an environment with JupyterLab at the --create-venv path. It changes no existing Python installation.
The kernel records absolute paths to the PHP binary, the Python interpreter, and juphyter. The PHP is the one running juphyter install, recorded as the first path on PATH that leads to it, such as /opt/homebrew/bin/php.
The second export puts the environment first on PATH, so jupyter lab and quarto render find it. When juphyter install used an existing environment, the directory does not exist and the line has no effect.

Without Composer’s bin directory on PATH, Composer can run the same command:
composer global exec juphyter -- install --create-venv ~/.venvs/juphyter
The command prints the kernelspec, the PHP, the Python, and the engine it recorded. When Quarto is installed and the Python Quarto would use has no Jupyter, it also prints a warning with the export line that fixes it. The kernel is still registered.

title: Installation
text:
Check the installation
juphyter doctor
juphyter doctor checks juphyter’s files, the PHP that runs the cells, the Python for the kernel, the Python Quarto will use, and every kernel juphyter registered. It changes nothing, and it ends with two summary lines:







Line
Meaning




JupyterLab: ready, with php.
The kernel is registered, and its PHP, Python, and juphyter files run.


Quarto: ready.
Quarto will run a Python that has Jupyter.


Quarto: not installed.
quarto is not on PATH. Quarto is needed only for rendering .qmd documents.


Quarto: not ready.
Quarto is installed and its Python lacks Jupyter or does not run. The report ends with the export line that fixes it.



A line marked fail makes the command exit 1, and Quarto: not ready. is a failure. A line marked warn, such as a missing pcntl, does not change the exit code.
Run juphyter doctor again after upgrading PHP or Python, or after removing a project or an environment. Troubleshooting covers the failures it reports.

title: Installation
text:
Keeping the PATH entries
Both export lines last until the shell closes. To keep the juphyter command in new shells, add Composer’s bin directory to your shell startup file. This appends to ~/.zshrc. Use ~/.bashrc for bash.
echo "export PATH=\"$(composer global config bin-dir --absolute):\$PATH\"" >> ~/.zshrc
Putting the Python environment in a startup file makes it the python3 for every program, including every Quarto project on the machine. Python interpreters and editors describes how to select it per editor workspace, per shell, or per Quarto project instead.

title: Installation
text:
The phpstats packages
juphyter does not depend on phibble, phplyr, or phiz. A notebook inside a Composer project that requires them can use them with the php kernel. To use them in notebooks outside any project, install them globally and register a second kernel that loads Composer’s global autoloader:
composer global require phpstats/phibble phpstats/phplyr phpstats/phiz
juphyter install --name phpstats --display-name "PHP (phpstats)" \
  --autoload "$(composer global config home)/vendor/autoload.php"
Documents name that kernel as jupyter: phpstats, and JupyterLab lists it as “PHP (phpstats)”. A kernel installed with --autoload always loads the autoloader it names, even for a notebook inside a Composer project, which is why it has its own name.

title: Installation
text:
Which classes a notebook sees
The kernel starts in the notebook’s directory, looks upward for vendor/autoload.php, and loads the first one it finds. A notebook anywhere inside a Composer project can use that project’s classes and packages.
Two settings replace that search. The more explicit one wins.

JUPHYTER_AUTOLOAD in the kernel’s environment. juphyter install --autoload PATH records it in the kernel.
A juphyter.json in the notebook’s directory or any directory above it.

A juphyter.json can also set the memory limit and the include path:
{
  "autoload": "vendor/autoload.php",
  "memory_limit": "512M",
  "include_path": "lib"
}
Relative paths resolve against the directory that holds juphyter.json.

title: Installation
text:
Installing into one project
juphyter can also be a development dependency of a project:
composer require --dev phpstats/juphyter
vendor/bin/juphyter install --name myproject

The kernel is still registered for your user, and it runs that project’s copy of juphyter.
Without --name, a second project’s install replaces the first project’s php kernel, and the command reports it as Replaced.
Deleting the project’s vendor directory breaks the kernel, which juphyter doctor reports.

title: Installation
text:
Several PHP versions
Give each kernel its own name:
juphyter install --name php83 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.3/bin/php
juphyter install --name php85 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.5/bin/php
JupyterLab then lists “PHP 8.3” and “PHP 8.5”. An absolute --php path is recorded as written. A bare name such as php8.4 is resolved to an absolute path, because a kernel cannot rely on PATH.

title: Installation
text:
Where the kernel is registered
juphyter install writes a kernelspec, the kernel.json file Jupyter reads to start a kernel, into the per-user Jupyter data directory. Every Jupyter installation on the machine searches that directory.







Platform
Directory




macOS
~/Library/Jupyter/kernels


Linux
$XDG_DATA_HOME/jupyter/kernels, or ~/.local/share/jupyter/kernels



JUPYTER_DATA_DIR replaces that directory, and --prefix PATH writes under PATH/share/jupyter instead.
juphyter uninstall --name NAME removes a kernel that juphyter registered. It refuses to remove a kernel of the same name that something else wrote, and so does a reinstall.

title: Installation
text:
Options
juphyter install --help lists every option:







Option
Meaning




--name NAME
The kernel’s name, which documents use in jupyter: NAME. Default: php.


--display-name TEXT
The label JupyterLab shows. Default: the PHP version, such as PHP 8.5.


--php PATH
The PHP binary that runs cells. Default: the PHP running juphyter install.


--python PATH
The Python that hosts the kernel. Default: the one that owns jupyter on PATH.


--prefix PATH
Write under PATH/share/jupyter.


--autoload PATH
Load this autoloader instead of searching above the notebook.


--create-venv PATH
Where to build a Python environment when none can host the kernel. Without it, the command asks, and builds one at ~/.venvs/juphyter when there is no terminal to ask.



juphyter --version prints the installed version and the PHP running it.

title: Limitations
text:
PHP cannot redeclare a class, interface, trait, enum, or function in the same kernel process. Restart the kernel before running a changed definition.
The kernel refuses such a cell before executing anything and names the collision:
RedeclarationError: The class, interface, trait or enum "Widget" was already
declared in this session, and PHP cannot redeclare it. Restart the kernel to
redefine it.

A cell that failed to declare anything leaves the name free. After class Widget extends Typo {} throws, the corrected cell runs.
Cells run out of order recover the same way. A subclass cell run before its base class fails, and runs once the base class cell has run.
A conditional declaration is bound at run time and is not refused:

if (! function_exists('helper')) {
    function helper() { /* ... */ }
}

title: Limitations
text:
PHP cannot redeclare a class, interface, trait, enum, or function in the same kernel process. Restart the kernel before running a changed definition.
The kernel refuses such a cell before executing anything and names the collision:
RedeclarationError: The class, interface, trait or enum "Widget" was already
declared in this session, and PHP cannot redeclare it. Restart the kernel to
redefine it.

A cell that failed to declare anything leaves the name free. After class Widget extends Typo {} throws, the corrected cell runs.
Cells run out of order recover the same way. A subclass cell run before its base class fails, and runs once the base class cell has run.
A conditional declaration is bound at run time and is not refused:

if (! function_exists('helper')) {
    function helper() { /* ... */ }
}

title: Limitations
section: A cell cannot declare a namespace
text:
A cell cannot declare a namespace
A namespace declaration is refused, because changing namespace part way through a session breaks name resolution for everything already defined. Use fully qualified names, or use statements, which carry from one cell to the next.

title: Limitations
section: Every cell runs under strict types
text:
Every cell runs under strict types
The kernel prepends declare(strict_types=1); to each cell.

A cell that declares strict_types=1 itself runs, and the kernel removes the duplicate.
declare(strict_types=0) and declare(encoding=...) are refused, because PHP accepts them only as a file’s first statement.
declare(ticks=...) is left alone.

title: Limitations
section: References and $this do not carry between cells
text:
References and $this do not carry between cells
Variables carry across cells by value. A reference taken in one cell is an ordinary copy in the next. $this has no meaning at a notebook’s top level. Objects, arrays, scalars, and resources persist normally.

title: Limitations
section: A closure called from another cell has no line in its traceback
text:
A closure called from another cell has no line in its traceback
A traceback names the cell and the line for functions and methods, across cells:
RuntimeException: from the function
  at Cell 1, line 3, in boom()
  at Cell 2, line 2
PHP’s trace does not say where a closure was declared, and every cell shares one file name, so a closure declared in one cell and called from another is reported without a location. The call site is still reported:
LogicException: from the closure
  in a closure
  at Cell 4, line 4

title: Limitations
section: A cell whose value is null shows no output
text:
A cell whose value is null shows no output
var_dump($x);, Juphyter\display($df), and any other call that returns nothing produce no Out[N]. Every other value is shown, including 0, false, '', [], and 'null'.

title: Limitations
section: exit and die end the kernel
text:
exit and die end the kernel
PHP cannot catch either, so the kernel process ends. The cell’s earlier output is shown, followed by:
SystemExit: The cell ended the kernel process with exit or die, so nothing
further can run. Restart the kernel to carry on.

title: Limitations
text:
Interrupting needs pcntl
The stop button sends a signal, so the PHP binary that runs the cells needs the pcntl extension with its functions callable. juphyter install and juphyter doctor warn when it is missing or listed in disable_functions. Enable pcntl for that binary, or run juphyter install --php with a binary that has it.
An interrupt arrives as Juphyter\Engine\Interrupt, which extends Error rather than Exception. A cell that catches Throwable in a loop can still swallow it.

title: Limitations
section: HTML tables format numbers differently from the text output
text:
HTML tables format numbers differently from the text output
A data frame’s text/plain output is phibble’s own. The HTML table formats a float with PHP’s string conversion instead of phibble’s significant-figure rules, so a dbl column can read differently in the two. Round values that are meant for display. The HTML header also omits the group count that the text output shows.

title: Limitations
text:
macOS and Linux only
The kernel interrupts a cell with POSIX signals, which the Windows PHP build does not provide, and the engine talks to the Python transport over a Unix socket. juphyter is tested on macOS and Linux. The Windows Subsystem for Linux has not been tested.

title: Limitations
text:
Not supported

Documentation on hover. Jupyter’s inspect_request is not answered, so shift-tab shows nothing.
Reading input. A cell cannot prompt, so readline() and fgets(STDIN) have nothing to read.
Magics. There are no %-prefixed commands.
Widgets. ipywidgets is not supported.
The debugger. Jupyter’s debug protocol is not implemented, so JupyterLab’s debugger does not attach.

title: Quarto
text: Render a .qmd document with PHP cells by naming the kernel in its front matter. No Quarto extension or other configuration is needed.

title: Quarto
text:
A minimal document
---
title: "Highway mileage"
jupyter: php
---

```{php}
$mpg = \Phibble\DataFrame::fromCsv('mpg.csv');
$mpg;
```

jupyter: php names the kernel by the --name that juphyter install was given. php is the default, and a kernel installed with --name php85 is named jupyter: php85.
A cell is a fenced block whose info string is {php}. It holds PHP without an opening tag.
Quarto runs the cells in order, in one PHP session per render.

Render it:
quarto render report.qmd
This writes report.html beside the document. --to chooses another format, such as --to typst for a PDF.
Quarto runs its Jupyter engine in a Python interpreter of its own choosing, which needs Jupyter in it. juphyter doctor reports whether it has one, and Python interpreters and editors covers how to choose it. CI tests Quarto 1.10.18.

title: Quarto
text:
Output formats



Format
Command
Extra requirement




HTML
quarto render report.qmd
None.


PDF through Typst
quarto render report.qmd --to typst
vl-convert for phiz plots.


PDF through LaTeX
quarto render report.qmd --to pdf
vl-convert for phiz plots, and rsvg-convert from librsvg.


Word
quarto render report.qmd --to docx
vl-convert for phiz plots. Without rsvg-convert, Pandoc warns and embeds the SVG as it is.



Typst ships inside Quarto and is the simpler PDF route. vl-convert produces the static SVG of a phiz plot. Put it on PATH, or point PHIZ_VL_CONVERT at it. Without it a plot has no SVG, and a PDF or Word document has no figure.
What each format takes from a cell’s output:








Format
A phiz plot
A phibble data frame




html
The interactive chart, drawn by Vega-Lite in the browser.
The HTML table, with the dimensions and the type row.


typst, pdf
The static SVG, as a numbered figure.
A typeset table, without the dimension note and the truncation footer.


ipynb
The HTML embed.
Nothing.



quarto render --to ipynb converts the rendered document, and Quarto’s conversion drops HTML tables and error outputs. Render to HTML or PDF when a document’s tables matter.

title: Quarto
text:
Cell options
Quarto’s cell options are #| comments at the top of a cell. PHP reads them as line comments.

#| echo: false runs the cell and hides its source.
#| eval: false shows the source and does not run it.
#| output: false runs the cell and shows no output.
#| error: true continues the render past a cell that throws, and keeps the traceback.
#| fig-cap: "..." captions the cell’s figure.
#| label: fig-mileage gives the figure a cross-reference label.

A captioned plot:

Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')->point(opacity: 0.5);






City against highway mileage.

title: Quarto
text:
Projects and autoloading
Quarto runs the kernel in the document’s directory. The kernel looks upward from there for vendor/autoload.php, so a document inside a Composer project can use that project’s classes and packages. A document outside any project names an autoloader with JUPHYTER_AUTOLOAD or a juphyter.json beside it. Which classes a notebook sees lists both.
In a Quarto project, each document names its kernel in its own front matter.

title: Quarto
text:
Freeze
execute: freeze: auto works with PHP documents. Quarto re-executes a document only when its source changes and stores the output in _freeze/. A project that commits that directory can be rendered without the packages the cells use, as long as a kernel with the document’s name is registered. Troubleshooting explains that requirement.
execute:
  freeze: auto
Each render of a PHP document starts a new PHP session. Quarto does not keep a PHP kernel alive between renders. Troubleshooting covers the details.
